keywords: New Gold Wave chinese cabbage variety
excerpt: New Gold Wave is a registered chinese cabbage variety. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1970. Takii bred it. It takes 48 to 56 days from transplanting to harvest.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

New Gold Wave chinese cabbage takes 48 to 56 days from transplanting to harvest. That is 5.2 days faster than the average of the 4 chinese cabbage varieties with a day count, 57.2 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit chinese cabbage fields most often: [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot), [black rot of cabbage](/diseases/black-rot), [cabbage webworm](/pests/cabbage-webworm), [clubroot](/diseases/clubroot), [diamondback moth](/pests/diamondback-moth). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Where and when to plant New Gold Wave chinese cabbage

Pechay Baguio heads best in cool places. In the lowlands, pick a heat tolerant hybrid and plant in the cool months. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items.q: Where can I buy seed of New Gold Wave?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
